About Sarabeth

A dream five years in the making

My name is Sarabeth, and I am honored to have been selected to represent Team USA at the Goalball Youth World Championships in Kazakhstan this November.

Goalball has been a huge part of my life for the past five years. Now I have the chance to compete against some of the best youth athletes in the world while proudly wearing the USA jersey.

While this is a dream come true for me, this fundraiser is about more than just my journey. I am part of an amazing team of six young women who have earned the opportunity to represent the United States on the international stage.

Together, we have trained, competed, and worked hard to reach this moment. Now we need your help to get there.

The Sport

What is Goalball?

Goalball is played by listening, not looking — here's what makes it one of the most demanding team sports in the Paralympic movement.

Paralympic Sport

Goalball is an official Paralympic sport, contested at the highest level of international competition.

Built for Blind & Low-Vision Athletes

It was designed specifically for athletes who are blind or visually impaired, leveling the playing field for everyone.

Blackout Eye Shades

Every player wears blackout shades, so the game is played entirely by sound and feel, regardless of vision level.

Teams of Three

Three athletes defend the full width of the court together, trusting each other completely.

A Ball Full of Bells

The ball has bells built inside it, so players track it purely by the sound it makes as it rolls.

Teamwork & Courage

Diving in front of a ball you cannot see takes real trust in your teammates and real courage.

Team Uniforms

Tournament Fees

Transportation

Good to Know

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Goalball?

Goalball is a Paralympic sport for blind and visually impaired athletes, played in teams of three with a bell-filled ball and blackout eye shades for every player.

Why is fundraising necessary?

International travel for a six-athlete team, including airfare, lodging, meals, uniforms, tournament fees, and transportation, comes at a real cost that falls on athletes and their families.

How are donations used?

Every donation goes directly toward getting Sarabeth and her teammates to Kazakhstan and covering the shared costs of competing at the Youth World Championships.

Can I share this page instead?

Absolutely. Sharing costs nothing and helps just as much — every share puts this fundraiser in front of someone new who might be able to help.

Is my donation tax deductible?

Donations are tax-deductible contributions to UNITED STATES ASSOCIATION OF BLIND ATHLETES, a 501(c)(3) registered nonprofit (EIN: 31-0977121).

Thank you for believing in Sarabeth and her Team USA teammates. Every dollar and every share carries this team one step closer to Kazakhstan.
